text:
tara: Heads-up — I'm proposing we try an adaptive DCGM exporter sampling + synthetic-inject experiment to reduce noisy ECC/Xid alerts and validate thresholds. Short thread with plan and rollback.

matt: Quick q — what do you mean by adaptive sampling? we already debounce.

tara: Two parts: 1) reduce raw per-card sample frequency during sustained high util windows (so we stop triggering on transient kernel noise), 2) run short synthetic Xid/ECC injections on canary nodes to calibrate alert thresholds objectively (measure precision/recall).

anya: 👍 Love the calibration idea. For alerting I'd prefer moving away from raw counts -> use normalized rates (errors / gpu_hour) and query quantiles (p95/p99) over a sliding window. That should be robust to different pod mixes.

matt: Agreed on normalization. Also watch for false negatives — if sampling drops too low we can miss real regressions. What's the plan to detect that?

tara: Plan summary:
- Canary: 2 racks (3 nodes per rack) in us-west1 with lower-risk tenants.
- Metric changes: DCGM exporter sample interval from 5s -> adaptive 5s/30s depending on node-util util windows.
- Alert rule: switch to a rate-based rule using increase() normalized by gpu_hours, and use 5m windows for canary then 15m cluster-wide.
- Calibration: run synthetic-inject script on canary that emits a controlled ECC/Xid pattern, measure how often alerts fire.
- Rollout: canary -> 25% -> full. Fail fast: auto rollback if we miss >50% of simulated injections or if real-production ECC rate rises >2x baseline.

Code (proposed recording + alert snippet):
```
# recording: per-card ecc rate normalized to gpu_hours
record: job:gpu_ecc_rate:per_card_per_hour
expr: increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[1h]) / (sum(node_gpu_hours_total) by (node))

# alert: p99 card-level error rate over 15m (cluster rule)
alert: HighGPUCardECCRate
expr: quantile_over_time(0.99, job:gpu_ecc_rate:per_card_per_hour[15m]) > 0.02
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-ecc-calibration
```

sylvia: How do we run injects safely? we need to ensure the tool only runs on canary nodes and doesn't affect shared storage or production jobs. Also cost: if our adaptive sampling causes extra drains, we might be losing capacity and paying replacement costs.

tara: Injection tool is `dcgm-sim` — it'll talk only to the exporter process and emit synthetic counters (no kernel faults). Example:
```
./dcgm-sim --target-node=node-uw1-canary-02 --card=0 --pattern=xid:seq:10:interval:30s --duration=10m
```
We will gate it behind an org-wide feature flag and explicit approval list. For capacity/cost: before rollout we'll run a short simulation of expected drains using historical ECC-triggered drains to estimate GPU-hours lost. If projected >= 4% of available GPU-hours we abort.

matt: Routing/ops: during canary set alert label to severity:critical -> route to #eng-oncall and #infra. For full rollout change back to severity:page but maintain a temporary low-noise dashboard. Also add an automated test that runs nightly compares dcgm exporter metrics vs kernel logs under /var/log/nv.

anya: Suggest adding a histogram-based metric in exporter (latency + errors) so we can threshold by quantile rather than absolute — much easier to tune per-hardware family.

tara: Good call. I'll add histogram buckets for error rates and expose family label (a100-v1, a100-v2, h100) so we can have per-family thresholds.

matt: Rollback steps captured?

tara: Yes — quick list:
1) flip sampling back to 5s fixed via config map: `kubectl -n infra set env deploy/dcgm-exporter SAMPLE_MODE=fixed SAMPLE_INTERVAL=5s`
2) disable synthetic injector via feature flag `dcgm.inject.enabled=false`
3) restore alerting rules from snapshot and escalate.
I'll paste exact commands in the runbook.

dcgm-bot: Synthetic calibration job scheduled for canary window 2024-11-05T02:00Z -> 02:30Z. Notifying infra@redwood.

sylvia: :thumbsup: sounds good — please add the simulation numbers and the list of canary node IDs to the runbook before we run.

anya: +1, also add a short postmortem template to capture calibration precision/recall results.

tara: Will do. I'll upload the runbook + prometheus rule PR by EOD and ping reviewers. Thanks all. :v:
